topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Per O.C.G.A. 43-40-22, what minimum balance must the Commission maintain in the real estate education, research, and recovery fund?
choice_a: $1 million
choice_d: $2 million
explanation: The commission shall maintain a minimum balance of $1 million in the real estate education, research, and recovery fund.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Under O.C.G.A. 43-40-22, if a single real estate transaction harms several different aggrieved persons, what is the maximum the recovery fund will pay out for that one transaction?
choice_a: $25,000, regardless of the number of persons aggrieved
choice_b: $25,000 per aggrieved person, with no overall cap
choice_c: $50,000, split evenly among the aggrieved persons
choice_d: There is no per-transaction limit, only a per-licensee limit
explanation: Recovery from the fund is capped at $25,000.00 per transaction regardless of the number of persons aggrieved by that transaction.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Per O.C.G.A. 43-40-22, once total payments from the recovery fund on behalf of a single licensee reach what amount, the fund's liability on behalf of that licensee ends?
choice_a: $75,000 in the aggregate
choice_b: $25,000 in the aggregate
choice_c: $100,000 in the aggregate
choice_d: There is no aggregate cap, only a per-transaction cap
explanation: The fund's liability terminates once aggregate payments on behalf of a licensee reach $75,000.00, in addition to the separate $25,000 per-transaction cap.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Under O.C.G.A. 43-40-22, an action for a judgment that could later result in an order for collection from the recovery fund must be started no later than how long after the cause of action accrues?
choice_a: Two years
choice_b: One year
choice_c: Four years
choice_d: Six years
explanation: No action for a judgment which subsequently results in an order for collection from the recovery fund may be started later than two years from the accrual of the cause of action.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Per O.C.G.A. 43-40-22, what happens to a licensee's license once the recovery fund pays out a claim on that licensee's behalf?
choice_a: The license is automatically revoked
choice_b: Nothing changes; the license remains active and in good standing
choice_c: The license is automatically suspended for exactly 90 days
choice_d: The license is placed on probation but remains active
explanation: When the fund pays a claim on behalf of a licensee, that licensee's license is automatically revoked.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Under O.C.G.A. 43-40-22, after the recovery fund pays a claim on a licensee's behalf, what financial obligation does that licensee owe to the fund?
choice_a: Repayment of the amount paid out, plus interest at the judgment rate
choice_b: No repayment obligation; recovery fund payments are non-recoverable by the Commission
choice_c: Repayment of only half the amount paid, interest-free
choice_d: Repayment is owed only if the licensee later reapplies for a new license
explanation: The licensee on whose behalf the fund made payment must repay to the fund the amount paid, plus interest at the judgment rate, with the Commission subrogated to the rights of the person who recovered.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Per O.C.G.A. 43-40-22, what must an applicant for an original real estate license pay in addition to the original license fee?
choice_a: A fee, in an amount established by the Commission, for deposit into the education, research, and recovery fund
choice_b: Nothing further; the original license fee already includes the recovery fund contribution
choice_c: A flat statutory fee of exactly $100, fixed in the Code itself
choice_d: A fee only if the applicant is applying for a broker's license
explanation: An applicant for an original license must pay, in addition to the original license fee, a fee for deposit in the recovery fund; the statute leaves the specific dollar amount to be established by Commission rule rather than fixing it in the Code section itself (hedge: exact current dollar figure not published in the statute).

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Under O.C.G.A. 43-40-22, to keep the recovery fund's minimum balance intact, the Commission may assess each licensee upon renewal an amount not to exceed how much per year?
explanation: The Commission may assess each licensee, upon renewal, an amount not to exceed $30.00 per year, if needed to maintain the fund's $1 million minimum balance.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Per O.C.G.A. 43-40-22, what happens to interest earned by the recovery fund on its lawfully invested balance?
choice_a: It is credited back to the fund and may be used for expanded educational and research purposes
choice_b: It reverts automatically to the state's general fund
choice_c: It is distributed pro rata to all currently licensed licensees
choice_d: It must remain uninvested and idle; the fund is barred from earning interest
explanation: The fund's assets may be legally invested, and interest earned is credited back to the recovery fund, supporting its expanded educational and research purposes.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Under O.C.G.A. 43-40-22, what type of damages may an aggrieved person recover from the recovery fund?
choice_a: Actual or compensatory damages, not including interest and costs
choice_b: Punitive damages only
choice_c: Interest and court costs only, with no recovery of the underlying loss
choice_d: Any damages a court awards, including punitive damages and attorney's fees
explanation: A person aggrieved by a licensee's chapter-violating conduct may recover actual or compensatory damages, not including interest and costs, subject to the fund's per-transaction and aggregate caps.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Per O.C.G.A. 43-40-22, which category of party is generally excluded from recovering against the fund?
choice_a: Bonding companies, except when they are principals in the real estate transaction at issue
choice_b: First-time home buyers
choice_c: Out-of-state residents
choice_d: Any person represented by an attorney
explanation: Any person aggrieved by a licensee's violation may recover from the fund, except bonding companies, when they are not principals in the real estate transaction.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Under O.C.G.A. 43-40-22, on what basis may a person recover from the recovery fund?
choice_a: An act, representation, transaction, or conduct of a licensee that violates Chapter 40
choice_b: Any financial loss connected to a real estate transaction, regardless of licensee fault
choice_c: Market losses caused by a general decline in property values
choice_d: Losses caused solely by unlicensed persons, since licensees are covered by their firm's insurance instead
explanation: Recovery is available to a person aggrieved by an act, representation, transaction, or conduct of a licensee that is in violation of Chapter 40, obtained by court order after suing the licensee.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Per O.C.G.A. 43-40-1, how is a 'community association manager' defined?
choice_a: A person who acts on behalf of a real estate broker in providing only community association management services
choice_b: Any officer of a homeowners' association board, whether licensed or not
choice_c: A person who independently manages community associations without needing to affiliate with a broker
choice_d: A synonym for 'property manager' with no separate licensure requirement
explanation: A 'community association manager' is a person who acts on behalf of a real estate broker in providing only community association management services -- a distinct, broker-affiliated license category.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Under the statutory definition in O.C.G.A. 43-40-1, may a licensed community association manager perform brokerage activities independently of any broker?
choice_a: No -- by definition, a CAM acts on behalf of a real estate broker and cannot operate independently
choice_b: Yes, once the CAM has five years of experience
choice_c: Yes, but only for community associations with fewer than 50 units
choice_d: Yes, provided the CAM posts a surety bond in lieu of broker affiliation
explanation: The statutory definition of 'community association manager' requires the person to act on behalf of a real estate broker; a CAM license does not authorize independent practice.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Per O.C.G.A. 43-40-8, what must an applicant for a community association manager's license furnish evidence of completing, in addition to passing a real estate examination?
choice_a: At least 25 instructional hours in a Commission-approved community association manager's course of study
choice_b: At least 75 instructional hours in a Commission-approved salesperson's course of study
choice_c: A four-year college degree in property management
choice_d: Two years of prior experience as a licensed salesperson
explanation: To qualify for a CAM license, an applicant must furnish evidence of completing at least 25 instructional hours in a Commission-approved community association manager's course of study and pass the real estate examination.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Per Rule 520-2-.04, the Community Association Managers Prelicense Course may devote no more than what percentage of required in-class time to testing?
choice_d: There is no limit on testing time
explanation: As with the other prelicense/postlicense courses, testing in the CAM Prelicense Course may not exceed 10% of the required in-class instructional time.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Per Rule 520-2-.04, which of the following is among the required core subject areas of the Community Association Managers Prelicense Course?
choice_a: Property law, forms of ownership, contracts, agency relationships, accounting practices, license law, and ethics
choice_b: Only physical facilities maintenance and landscaping techniques
choice_c: Only federal tax preparation for community associations
choice_d: Only general business math with no legal content
explanation: The CAM Prelicense Course curriculum covers property law, forms of ownership, contracts, agency relationships, accounting practices, license law, ethics, environmental laws, and safety, among other core subjects.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Per Rule 520-2-.04, what is the minimum number of instructional hours required for the Brokers Prelicense Course?
choice_a: 60 instructional hours
choice_b: 75 instructional hours
choice_c: 25 instructional hours
choice_d: 100 instructional hours
explanation: The Brokers Prelicense Course requires a minimum of 60 instructional hours (whether taught in-class or by computer-based delivery).

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Per Rule 520-2-.04, in addition to reviewing Salespersons Prelicense material, what advanced content must the Brokers Prelicense Course cover?
choice_a: Loan closings, office management, personnel policies, trust accounting, and broker responsibility for affiliated licensees
choice_b: Only advanced appraisal mathematics
choice_c: Only federal securities law as applied to real estate investment trusts
choice_d: Nothing beyond the Salespersons Prelicense material; the two courses are identical in content
explanation: Beyond reviewing Salespersons Prelicense material at a more advanced level, the Brokers Prelicense Course must address loan closings, office management, personnel policies, trust accounting, and broker responsibility for affiliated licensees.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Per Rule 520-2-.04, testing in the Salespersons Prelicense Course is limited to what maximum percentage of the required classroom (or computer-based-equivalent) time?
choice_d: No specific percentage limit applies
explanation: As with the other approved prelicense/postlicense courses, testing in the Salespersons Prelicense Course may not exceed 10% of required class time.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Per Rule 520-2-.04, which topic is specifically required content in the Salespersons Prelicense Course curriculum?
choice_a: Mortgage fraud identification, fair housing, and antitrust laws
choice_b: Advanced commercial loan underwriting only
choice_c: International real estate investment treaties
choice_d: Community association reserve-fund actuarial analysis
explanation: The Salespersons Prelicense Course curriculum specifically requires coverage of topics including mortgage fraud identification, fair housing laws, and antitrust laws, along with contracts, conveyances, closings, agency disclosure, pricing, and financing.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Per Rule 520-2-.04, what is the minimum number of instructional hours required for the Sales Postlicense Course?
choice_a: 25 instructional hours
choice_b: 40 instructional hours
choice_c: 50 instructional hours
choice_d: 10 instructional hours
explanation: The Sales Postlicense Course (the course new salespersons must complete within their first year of licensure) requires a minimum of 25 instructional hours, with testing likewise capped at 10% of that time.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Per Rule 520-2-.04, what does the Sales Postlicense Course curriculum focus on?
choice_a: Legal fundamentals and basic practices in residential, agricultural, commercial, or industrial property sales or management
choice_b: Exclusively appraisal licensing prerequisites
choice_c: Exclusively construction-defect litigation procedure
choice_d: Exclusively community association reserve-study methodology
explanation: The Sales Postlicense Course curriculum focuses on legal fundamentals and basic practices across residential, agricultural, commercial, and industrial property sales or management, and, for residential-focused courses, includes mortgage fraud identification content.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Under O.C.G.A. 43-40-8, a person previously licensed only as a community association manager who now wants to qualify as a broker must complete which additional education, beyond the standard broker's course of study?
choice_a: The 75-hour Salespersons Prelicense Course (or equivalent additional college coursework)
choice_b: No additional education; the 25-hour CAM course satisfies the salesperson-level prerequisite
choice_c: An additional 25-hour CAM refresher course only
choice_d: A separate 100-hour appraisal course
explanation: Because a CAM's 25-hour prelicense course does not cover general salesperson-level content, a CAM applying for a broker's license must additionally complete the 75-hour Salespersons Prelicense Course, or equivalent additional college coursework, on top of the broker's course of study.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Under Rule 520-1-.05, how many total instructional hours of continuing education must an active licensee -- including a community association manager -- complete during each four-year renewal period?
choice_a: 36 instructional hours
choice_b: 24 instructional hours
choice_c: 18 instructional hours
choice_d: 12 instructional hours
explanation: Effective July 1, 2015, active licensees -- associate brokers, salespersons, and community association managers alike -- must complete 36 instructional hours of continuing education during each four-year renewal period to keep an active license.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Per Rule 520-1-.05, of the 36 required continuing education hours per renewal period, how many hours must specifically cover the topic of license law?
choice_a: At least 3 hours
choice_b: At least 12 hours
choice_c: At least 1 hour
choice_d: License law content is not a required CE topic
explanation: Effective July 1, 2016, at least 3 of the 36 required continuing education hours per renewal period must be on the topic of license law.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Per Rule 520-2-.04, an individual approved continuing education course offering must consist of at least how many credit hours?
choice_a: Three credit hours
choice_b: One credit hour
choice_c: Six credit hours
choice_d: Twelve credit hours
explanation: An approved continuing education course must be structured to provide at least three credit hours of instruction, distinct from the separate 36-hour total requirement per four-year renewal period.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Under O.C.G.A. 43-40-8, is a licensee required to take an examination to receive credit for continuing education courses completed toward license renewal?
choice_a: No -- no examination is required for continuing education taken for renewal purposes
choice_b: Yes -- every CE course must end with a Commission-proctored exam
choice_c: Yes, but only for CE courses on license law
choice_d: Yes, but only for community association managers
explanation: Unlike prelicense and postlicense courses, no examination is required for continuing education courses taken to satisfy license renewal requirements.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Under O.C.G.A. 43-40-8, within what time frame must a newly licensed salesperson complete the required 25-hour post-license course of study?
choice_a: Within one year of the issuance of the license
choice_b: Within 30 days of the issuance of the license
choice_c: Within five years of the issuance of the license
choice_d: There is no deadline as long as the license remains active
explanation: A newly licensed salesperson must complete an approved 25-hour post-license course of study within one year of the license's issuance; failing to do so causes the license to lapse.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Under O.C.G.A. 43-40-8, if a salesperson enrolled in the required post-license course within the one-year deadline but had not finished it when the license lapsed, how long does that salesperson have to complete the course and reinstate the license?
choice_a: Within six months of the lapsing of the license
choice_b: Within 90 days of the lapsing of the license
choice_c: Within two years of the lapsing of the license
choice_d: There is no reinstatement option once the license lapses
explanation: A salesperson who was enrolled in, but had not completed, the approved post-license course within the original one-year window may reinstate by completing that course within six months of the license's lapsing.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Under O.C.G.A. 43-40-8, a salesperson whose license lapsed WITHOUT having enrolled in the post-license course in time must do what to reinstate?
choice_a: Complete 25 instructional hours in a new approved course and pay whatever penalty fees the Commission requires by rule
choice_b: Simply pay a late fee; no additional coursework is required
choice_c: Retake only the state portion of the licensing examination, with no coursework
choice_d: Wait out a mandatory two-year cooling-off period before any reinstatement is possible
explanation: A salesperson who missed the enrollment window must complete 25 instructional hours in a new approved course and pay applicable penalty fees under Commission rules before applying to reinstate the license.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Per Rule 520-2-.03, before being approved, a prospective real estate instructor must complete which prerequisite courses?
choice_a: A Commission-approved instructor development workshop and a Salespersons Prelicense Course
choice_b: Only a general adult-education teaching certificate
choice_c: Only the Brokers Prelicense Course, with no instructor-specific training
choice_d: No prerequisite courses are required, only five years of real estate sales experience
explanation: An approved-instructor applicant must complete a Commission-approved instructor development workshop and a Salespersons Prelicense Course, in addition to other real-estate-background and criminal-history requirements.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Per Rule 520-2-.03, under what circumstance may the Commission approve a nonresident instructor?
choice_a: If another jurisdiction's real estate regulatory body has approved the person and the person has actively taught approved prelicense courses for at least five years
choice_b: Nonresident instructors may never be approved to teach Georgia real estate courses
choice_c: Automatically, as long as the person holds any teaching license from any U.S. state
choice_d: Only if the nonresident instructor also holds a Georgia broker's license
explanation: The Commission may approve a nonresident instructor whom another jurisdiction's real estate regulatory body has already approved, provided the person can show at least five years of active teaching experience as an approved prelicense instructor.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Per Rule 520-2-.02, a real estate school's application must include compliance statements addressing which of the following, in addition to course outlines and instructor lists?
choice_a: ADA compliance, nondiscrimination, and electronic registration capability
choice_b: The school's projected annual profit margin
choice_c: A list of the school's competitors in the local market
choice_d: The personal home addresses of all enrolled students
explanation: An approved-school application must include, among other items, compliance statements regarding ADA compliance, nondiscrimination, and electronic registration capability, along with detailed course outlines with learning objectives and instructor lists.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Per Rule 520-2-.02, who is responsible for certifying that a student has completed a school's course?
choice_a: The school director and/or coordinator
choice_b: Any individual instructor, without director/coordinator involvement
choice_c: The Commission itself certifies every student's completion directly
choice_d: The student's sponsoring broker
explanation: The school director and/or coordinator is responsible for certifying student completion of all courses offered by the school.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Per Rule 520-2-.02, what ongoing duty does a school coordinator or director have regarding the school's instructors?
choice_a: To conduct consistent and regular evaluation of the school's instructors and provide students an opportunity for unsigned written evaluations
choice_b: No ongoing evaluation duty exists once an instructor is initially approved by the Commission
choice_c: To personally re-teach a portion of every course alongside each instructor
choice_d: To evaluate instructors only if a formal student complaint is filed
explanation: Coordinators and directors must conduct consistent and regular evaluation of the school's instructors and give students the opportunity to complete unsigned written evaluations of instructors.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Per Rule 520-1-.06, when is a broker providing community association management services exempt from maintaining fidelity bond or insurance coverage for a given association's funds?
choice_a: Only if the broker never handles, for that association, funds exceeding $60,000
choice_b: Only if the association has fewer than ten member units
choice_c: Community association managers are always exempt from any bonding or insurance requirement
choice_d: Only if the association's governing documents expressly waive the requirement
explanation: A broker providing community association management services must maintain fidelity bond or insurance coverage at all times, unless the broker never handles funds for that community association exceeding $60,000.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Per Rule 520-1-.06, the minimum fidelity bond or insurance coverage a broker must maintain for community association funds must equal at least what?
choice_a: Three months' assessments due from all members, plus reserve funds
choice_b: One month's assessments due from all members, with no reserve-fund component
choice_c: A flat $10,000, regardless of the association's size
choice_d: The broker's own annual gross commission income
explanation: Required fidelity coverage must equal at least three months' assessments due from all members of the community association, plus any reserve funds, and must cover the maximum amount of funds the broker collects, maintains, controls, has access to, or disburses.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Per Rule 520-1-.06, who must be named as an additional named insured on a community association management fidelity bond or insurance policy?
choice_a: The community association(s) covered by the policy
choice_b: The individual homeowner who pays the highest assessment
choice_c: The Georgia Real Estate Commission itself
choice_d: No additional named insured is required; the broker's name alone suffices
explanation: The required fidelity bond or insurance policy must name the community association(s) as an additional named insured.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Per Rule 520-1-.06, besides the broker itself, whom must community association fidelity bond/insurance coverage extend to?
choice_a: All partners, officers, licensed affiliates, and employees of the broker
choice_b: Only the broker's spouse, if also a licensee
choice_c: Only unlicensed clerical staff
choice_d: Only the specific individual who signed the management agreement
explanation: Required fidelity bond or insurance coverage must extend to the broker and all of the broker's partners, officers, licensed affiliates, and employees.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Per Rule 520-1-.06, how many community associations may a single fidelity bond or insurance policy generally cover?
choice_a: A broker must generally maintain a separate fidelity bond or insurance policy for each community association, absent a Commission-approved alternative
choice_b: One policy may always cover an unlimited number of associations with no restriction
choice_c: A single policy may cover up to five associations, but no more
choice_d: Coverage is pooled automatically across all of a broker's managed associations by operation of law
explanation: A broker must generally maintain a separate fidelity bond or fidelity insurance policy for each community association it manages, unless the broker obtains Commission-approved alternative coverage.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Per Rule 520-1-.06, what documentation obligation does a broker have regarding a community association's fidelity bond or insurance policy?
choice_a: The broker must retain copies of the policy and certificates and provide a copy to the community association
choice_b: No documentation retention obligation exists once coverage is bound
choice_c: The broker must destroy the policy documents at the end of each policy year
choice_d: Only the insurer, not the broker, is required to keep policy records
explanation: The broker must retain copies of the fidelity bond or insurance policy and any certificates, and must provide a copy of that documentation to the community association.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Per Rule 520-1-.06, apart from the shorter notice period for cancellation due to non-payment of premiums, how much prior written notice must generally be given before a community association fidelity bond or policy is cancelled or substantially modified?
choice_a: Thirty days
choice_b: Fifteen days
choice_c: Sixty days
choice_d: No notice is required in any circumstance
explanation: Outside the ten-day non-payment exception, an insurer may not cancel or substantially modify a community association fidelity bond or policy without giving thirty days' prior written notice.

topic: Real Estate Education, Course Standards & Community Association Management
question: Per Rule 520-1-.06, a community association fidelity bond or insurance policy must be issued by what kind of company?
choice_a: An insurance company authorized to write such bonds or policies in Georgia
choice_b: Any insurance company, regardless of state authorization, as long as it is nationally accredited
choice_c: Only a company wholly owned by the community association itself
choice_d: Only the same insurer that carries the broker's own errors-and-omissions coverage
explanation: The required fidelity bond or insurance policy must be issued by an insurance company authorized to write such bonds or policies in Georgia.
